root_cause.text: The i915 GT heartbeat code in `intel_engine_heartbeat.c` released `engine->heartbeat.systole` with a non-atomic read-plus-clear (`engine->heartbeat.systole` / `fetch_and_zero()`), allowing the heartbeat worker and `intel_engine_park_heartbeat()` to race and both `i915_request_put()` the same request, causing a refcount underflow/use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says the worker “reads `engine->heartbeat.systole` and calls `i915_request_put()` on it… but clears the pointer in a separate, non-atomic step,” and `intel_engine_park_heartbeat()` can “read the stale non-NULL systole pointer and calls `i915_request_put()` on it again”; the patch fixes this by replacing both sites with `xchg(&engine->heartbeat.systole, NULL)`, making the pointer handoff atomic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Make heartbeat systole handling atomic to avoid races and preserve the request until completion.
intent_record.what: The code that reads and clears `engine->heartbeat.systole` in `heartbeat()` was changed from a direct load followed by a conditional clear to an atomic `xchg(&engine->heartbeat.systole, NULL)`. The completion check and `i915_request_put(rq)` remain, but if the request is not completed, the pointer is written back to `engine->heartbeat.systole`.
intent_record.how: This makes access to `heartbeat.systole` atomic and avoids races where multiple contexts could observe or modify the pointer concurrently. It preserves the request reference until completion is confirmed, while restoring the pointer when the request is still active so the heartbeat state is not lost.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix heartbeat request cleanup by atomically nulling and releasing `engine->heartbeat.systole` only when present.
intent_record.what: The single-line conditional cleanup at the end of `heartbeat()` was expanded into a block: instead of directly calling `i915_request_put(fetch_and_zero(&engine->heartbeat.systole))`, the code now uses `rq = xchg(&engine->heartbeat.systole, NULL);` and conditionally calls `i915_request_put(rq)` only if `rq` is non-NULL.
intent_record.how: This changes the heartbeat teardown path to atomically clear `engine->heartbeat.systole` before releasing the request, making the pointer exchange explicit and avoiding a release call on a potentially stale value. Functionally, it preserves the cleanup behavior while improving correctness/safety of the request handoff at the end of the heartbeat cycle.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix heartbeat parking to safely clear and release the stored request reference using an atomic exchange before dropping it.
intent_record.what: In `intel_engine_park_heartbeat()`, the single-line conditional that cancelled delayed work and immediately released `engine->heartbeat.systole` via `fetch_and_zero()` was expanded into a block that first assigns `xchg(&engine->heartbeat.systole, NULL)` to a local `rq` pointer and then calls `i915_request_put(rq)` only if `rq` is non-NULL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the heartbeat parking path still cancels the delayed work, but it now clears the `systole` pointer using an atomic exchange and avoids passing a potentially NULL or concurrently modified pointer directly into `i915_request_put()`. This makes the teardown of the heartbeat request reference safer and better synchronized with concurrent updates.

consistency_review.core_intent: Make heartbeat request cleanup atomic by safely clearing and releasing the stored request reference only when present.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: they make heartbeat systole cleanup atomic so the worker and park path cannot both drop the same request reference, preventing the refcount underflow/use-after-free race.

candidates.rationale: This is the non-atomic read of the shared heartbeat request pointer. Because it is later cleared separately, the heartbeat worker can race with parking/cleanup and both end up putting the same request.
This is the release of the request that becomes unsafe when combined with the separate, racy clear of engine->heartbeat.systole; concurrent cleanup can double-put the same request.
This separate clear after the put is the core race window: another path may observe the old pointer and also call i915_request_put(), causing refcount underflow/use-after-free.
This line shows the intended fix pattern replacing the vulnerable read-plus-clear; the pre-fix vulnerability came from not using this atomic fetch-and-zero behavior.
This is the corrected atomic release used in parking; it highlights that the vulnerable pre-fix code had a non-atomic put-and-clear sequence that could race with the worker.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the non-atomic read of the shared heartbeat request pointer. It participates in the read-plus-clear race that allowed the worker and parking path to both act on the same request.
This drops the request reference after the racy read of engine->heartbeat.systole, so a concurrent cleaner can also put the same request and trigger refcount underflow/use-after-free.
This separate clear occurs after the put instead of atomically exchanging the pointer, creating the race window where another path can observe the stale pointer and double-put it.
